Static fallback also gained the missing `emitGeneratedRenderClass` call (hierarchy-less XLU meshes were staying opaque). Both `ROMEXTRACT_PDMESH_OBJ_EXPORT_VERSION_LABEL` + `ROMEXTRACT_PDMESH_FAST_CACHE_KIND` bumped `_vtxcolour` to force re-extraction. Back-compat: an archive with no colour tokens, or an all-white mesh, collapses to a single white entry — rendered output identical to today (the on-vertex byte changes 0xffffffff→0x00 = a valid index-0 white reference instead of relying on the B-937 out-of-range fallback). >64 distinct colours clamp to nearest with a one-line warning. gfx_pc.cpp crash guard left untouched (defense-in-depth). | `port/src/romextract_pdmesh.c`, `port/src/modasset_compiler.c` | NOT yet built. The real picture: her textures are a MIX -- bright tan SKIN + genuinely-DARK combat SUIT (uniform 0x101010 = 16,16,16 RGBA32). So `MODULATEIA = TEXEL0 x lit-shade` gives ~11 on the dark suit (16 x ~0.7) and bright on skin -- but the body measures ~6-9, darker than even that, and the bright skin isn't prominent. The stock path renders her visible by the 2-cycle CUSTOM_17/18 ENV-blend lifting the dark suit -- but renderdata->envcolour is 0 in this menu-backdrop context (exactly why letting Type3 stand earlier went PURE BLACK). So "make her bright like the original" hinges on the ENV layer (set/lift the env for the chr render, then the CUSTOM_17/18 env-blend works), plus a check on why the tan-skin areas don't read brighter. Deep, multi-factor; pinned but not closed. **ENV-LIFT RESOLVED 2026-06-24 (she now renders LIT + TEXTURED isolated, no longer a silhouette):** Traced the stock chr env path (`--debug-chr-env` at chr.c:3766): the stock does NOT use a bright env -- env=`var80062a48`={64,10,10} (a dark-red tint), and the real lift is the per-chr room shade carried in FOG (`fogcolour=colour`, ramping ~0->127+) under 2-cycle `G_CC_CUSTOM_17/18` (mux from gbiex.h: cyc1 `(TEXEL0-ENV)*shade_alpha+ENV`, cyc2 `COMBINED*SHADE`) + `G_RM_FOG_PRIM_A`. The generated DL can't carry that per-vertex fog. Replication (modasset_compiler.c, mcount==3, gated by new `s_genLitChrBody`): keep G_LIGHTING (lit-shade form); let the stock 2-cycle CUSTOM_17/18 stand (per-material emitters only enable texturing, no 1-cycle/MODULATEIA override); supply the lift via a DERIVED env (mid-grey 160) + DERIVED mid shade_alpha (140 on the colour table) so texture+env both contribute -> `[lerp(TEXEL0,160,0.55)]*lit_shade`. **CRITICAL FINDING: the stock `FOG_PRIM_A` render mode WASHES her to PURE BLACK in a backdrop context where the room-shade fog is near-black** -- measured: 1-cycle MODULATEIA read 6-9, but letting stock 2-cycle FOG_PRIM_A stand read 0 (full silhouette). Fix: override the render mode to `G_RM_PASS, G_RM_AA_ZB_OPA_SURF2` (fog-independent opaque 2-cycle) for generated chr bodies. RESULT (`main_menu_joanna_envlift`, room hidden, screenshot `.../20260624T131042-main_menu_joanna_envlift/002-envlift_b.png`): tan SKIN on the raised arm + blue-grey combat SUIT with visible form + panel detail = textured Joanna, lit, correct geometry/pose (leaning at the terminal). CAVEATS: env/alpha are DERIVED (not stock); fog is disabled for generated chr bodies (distant ones won't fade into scene fog); affects ALL mcount==3 generated bodies incl gameplay (more readable + fog-independent, not eyeballed in-game). **SCENE-DESYNC ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED 2026-06-24 (VAO/VBO unbind in a CORE profile -- she now RENDERS at her terminal with the room):** instrumented the GL state the raw-GL scenarioSceneRendererRender leaves (`--debug-scene-glstate` at its exit) AND the state of Joanna's actual draw (`--debug-firstdraw-glstate` in gfx_opengl_draw_triangles). Ruled out WITH DATA (not guesses): depth (a scissor-safe glClear(GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT) after the scene renderer did NOT reveal her), scissor (her draw box=(0,90,1920,817), full), colormask (1111), blend (off), cull (off), FBO (1, same as the room), array-buffer (added a save/restore of GL_ARRAY_BUFFER_BINDING to the scene renderer -- hygiene, not the cause). Smoking gun: a force-prim run showed her FULL body batches reaching glDrawArrays (tris=220+) with DEPTH=GL_ALWAYS yet ZERO magenta pixels, while her CPU clip (CLIPDBG) was correct + onscreen (ndc ~(-0.07,0.05)). GPU rasterised nothing despite a correct CPU transform = the GPU read different vertices than fast3d computed. Cause: this is a **core profile** build (GLSL 430 core); fast3d binds its `opengl_vao`+`opengl_vbo` ONCE at init and assumes they persist, but gfx_opengl_draw_triangles uploads+draws with no rebind. The scene renderer binds its own VAO/VBO and leaves `vao=0` on return -- and in a core profile, drawing with VAO 0 reads NO attrib pointers, so her geometry rasterised nothing. **FIX:** rebind `opengl_vao`+`opengl_vbo` at the top of gfx_opengl_draw_triangles so every fast3d draw is self-sufficient regardless of external GL state (correctness > the per-batch bind cost; future-proofs against any raw-GL renderer). RESULT (`main_menu_joanna_full`, full backdrop, screenshot `.../20260624T135156-main_menu_joanna_full/002-full_b.png`): Joanna renders textured + lit, reaching toward the green-monitor desk PC (`base:model_goodpc`) -- SHE IS AT HER TERMINAL. **REMAINING (separate compositing layer, not the desync): the room WALLS are blue.** The scene renderer's room (`base:scenario_citraining`, 28848 verts) DOES render, but fast3d's fullscreen background draw -- previously a no-op because fast3d was wholly broken at vao=0, now drawing after the VAO fix -- covers it. So fixing the desync revealed the scene-renderer room was only ever "visible" because fast3d couldn't draw. **MONEY SHOT LANDED 2026-06-24 (tiled CI room backdrop + Joanna at her terminal):** the blue bg fill = `skyRender` (sky.c:266), which under `!clouds_enabled` (indoor CITRAINING) switches to `G_CYC_FILL` and `gDPFillRectangle`s the whole viewport with `env->sky_{r,g,b}` (blue) -- a fullscreen depth-off fill drawn first in the world DL (lv.c:1658, with G_ZBUFFER cleared). After the VAO fix made fast3d draw, that fill covered the scene renderer room. FIX: gate the `skyRender` call on `!scenarioSceneRendererIsActive()` (lv.c:1658) so the scene-renderer's tiled room is the backdrop when it provides one. RESULT (`main_menu_joanna_moneyshot`, screenshot `.../20260624T141035-main_menu_joanna_moneyshot/002-shot_55.png` + zoom `joanna_zoom.png`): tiled CI room (tan walls, ceiling lights, blue floor) + the desk PC (green monitor) + Joanna textured/lit AT HER TERMINAL. **B-936 (Joanna-not-appearing) is CRACKED -- 4 root causes, all fixed on dev: fovy=0 projection (299a0628), G_LIGHTING (6da0e831), env-lift + fog-independent (23ac8e6d), VAO/VBO scene-desync (bc86441f), sky-fill gate (08d32a45).** **NEW SEPARATE ISSUE (see B-942): her held POSE is skeletally DISTORTED** -- a thin spike-limb shoots off-body + the torso is contorted (not a natural lean). All held frames (40-85s) byte-identical (the menu freezes the cutscene frame). The MODEL + TEXTURES are correct (zoom verifies the blue-grey combat suit + tan skin + torso proportions = it IS Joanna), but the pose is wrong. The spike is the signature of a bone-weight/transform bug in the generated chr body (nummatrices=19), observable only now that she renders. So the render arc is closed; the skeletal/animation pose is the next layer. CAUTION: the build wrapper (build-headless.ps1) REPORTS "Result: SUCCESS" even when a source file fails to compile and ninja stops (the stale binary stays) -- ALWAYS verify (diagnostic string in Build/PerfectDark.exe, or binary relink mtime) before trusting a run. |

Worst-case wire load at SWARM_GPU_MAX=4096 is ~80 KB / 100 ms = ~800 KB/s, split into 4 chunks of 1024 bots each (~20 KB per chunk) on the unreliable channel so any single packet stays below ENet's recommended ceiling. A future slice can shift the compute to CPU on dedicated and broadcast the same SVC opcode, OR add a "headless GPU" path that runs the compute via a headless GL context.  (b) **No client-side prediction.** Remote clients render the host's snapshot directly. At 10 Hz broadcasts on lossy links, position can visibly jitter; per-frame extrapolation from the wire'd velocity is a small follow-up. The vel field is already on the wire so the receiver has everything it needs to extrapolate.  (c) **Lossy compression tuning.** s16 cm pos / vel and s8 ratio up are chosen to fit arena scale; tighter packing (e.g. range-relative pos quantization per-broadcast) is unexplored. (d) **Full-pool broadcast even when low ladder count is active.** The state texture is sized SWARM_GPU_MAX-wide; we broadcast all 4096 columns every frame even when only 8 bots are alive. The receiver dequant + uploads the zeroed pad columns harmlessly. A future slice can plumb the live `count` through `swarmGpuStateGetCount()` and broadcast only the active prefix.  (e) **Unreliable channel only.** If a packet is dropped, that frame's snapshot is lost; the next 10 Hz tick supersedes it. | **B-332** | CRITICAL | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-05-16 (c029, dev).** GPU swarm cycler `FATAL: ACCESS_VIOLATION` in `chrRemove(prop->chr=NULL)` when the apply loop routed through `chrSetPosWithCachedGround` (Track 1+5 Slice 3 ship, commit `937bfc9b`). Original Track 1+5 worker hypothesis pointed at the omitted `chrMoveToPos` pre-flight (`propDeregisterRooms` + `chr0f0220ac` room re-register) and shipped a conservative fallback that kept `chrSetPos(findground=true)` in the apply loop — saving the surface_up sampler raycast only, ~20% raycast reduction at 512 bots vs the 80% Slice-3 target. Two-stage root cause: (a) `chrSetPosWithCachedGround` gated `propDeregisterRooms + roomsCopy + chr0f0220ac` behind an `if (newrooms)` check that compared the caller's `rooms` array against `chr->prop->rooms`. The swarm apply loop passes `chr->prop->rooms` back to itself, so `newrooms` was ALWAYS false and the room trio NEVER ran — bots drifting across room boundaries had stale `prop->rooms` entries. (b) `chrSetPosWithCachedGround` did not set `CHRCFLAG_FORCETOGROUND`. `chrMoveToPos` sets it every call (line 15780); the bondwalk fall path (`chr.c:920`) consumes the flag and SNAPS the chr to its ground level, bypassing the fall accumulator. Without the flag, the swarm bots ran the fall path every frame. The cached ground (sampled at the bot's previous frame position) didn't match the bot's just-applied position; the `chrTickBg` path's own cdFindGroundInfoAtCyl (computed at the new pos) could yield ground<-100000 if the bot drifted over a void, and after a few frames `manground <= -30000` triggered the pit-death branch at chr.c:940. For chrs without `aibot` set — the GPU swarm population — the off-map fallback at chr.c:881-902 does NOT apply (it gates on `chr->aibot != NULL`), so the chr fell unchecked, `chr->hidden |= CHRHFLAG_DELETING` fired, the next `chrTick` called `chrRemove` + returned `TICKOP_FREE`, the prop tick dispatcher freed the prop (`prop->chr = NULL`), and `s_Swarm[i].chr` was left pointing at a freed prop. The cycler's `despawn_all` then AVed on the NULL `prop->chr` deref. Fix: (1) `chrSetPosWithCachedGround` runs the `propDeregisterRooms + roomsCopy + chr0f0220ac` trio UNCONDITIONALLY (drop the `newrooms` gate) so a caller passing `chr->prop->rooms` back to itself still gets a correct rooms re-resolve via `bgFindEnteredRooms` on the just-written `prop->pos`. (2) `chrSetPosWithCachedGround` sets `chr->chrflags \|= CHRCFLAG_FORCETOGROUND` every call, mirroring `chrMoveToPos`. (3) Swarm apply loop in `port/fast3d/swarm_gpu.cpp::swarmGpuStepAndApply` re-routes through `chrSetPosWithCachedGround` using `s_FloorCache[i].ground/floorcol/floortype/floorroom` populated by the pre-pass; both `chrSetPos`-internal raycasts skipped on cache hit AND miss (the miss path's cdFindGroundInfoAtCyl already runs in the pre-pass). Raycast budget at 512 bots / 78% hit rate: 226 raycasts/frame vs 1536 baseline = **85% reduction** (target was 80%). At 768 bots / 87% hit rate: 204 raycasts/frame vs 2304 baseline = **91% reduction**. The cached helper is now a safe drop-in for the per-frame-per-bot apply pattern. Class: same family as B-264 / B-307b (init-vs-init drift — a derived helper omits an invariant the legacy entry point quietly enforced). Per `feedback_no_half_measures`, fix at the helper layer, not at the caller. | `src/game/chraction.c::chrSetPosWithCachedGround`; `port/fast3d/swarm_gpu.cpp::swarmGpuStepAndApply` apply loop | Build verify: 4-target clean (`ninja -C Build pd pd-server pd-tests Updater.exe` PASS; PerfectDark.exe 55.7 MB rebuilt 2026-05-16; pd-server/pd-tests/Updater.exe unchanged because chraction.c is not linked into those targets). | **B-330** | CRITICAL | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-05-16 (c029, dev).** Root cause: `roomGetProps()` (`src/game/prop.c:3602`) declared a `len` parameter for the caller-supplied propnums buffer, but the implementation IGNORED `len` and wrote `writeptr++` until every chunk in every iterated room was drained. Every caller passes a 256-element stack-allocated `s16 propnums[256]` plus `len=256`. When a single room contains >=256 unique props -- exactly the case during the CPU swarm benchmark at the 128 -> 256 and 256 -> 512 ladder cycles (256 / 512 Skedars sharing the player's room) -- the writes spilled past the caller's stack buffer, scribbling over local variables, return addresses, and the MSVC `/GS` stack cookie. The cookie check at the caller's epilogue (chrTick / bot.c / collision.c / chraicommands.c / propobj.c / chraction.c / etc., all 24 call sites) detected the corruption and raised `STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN` (0xC0000409, `__fastfail`) -- a Windows kernel-level abort with no SEH unwind, no FATAL line, no breadcrumb. This is the silent process-death class Mike's playtest log captured at 256 -> 512 (`Build/pd-client.1.log`, 2026-05-16: despawn_all freed 254 chrs, then process killed before respawn_ring logged its `target=512` line). It is the SAME root cause class as the previously-thought-fixed B-307 (CHRVTX pool bump in `715424c4` was a real fix for a DIFFERENT symptom -- the GBI opcode 0xbb0000ff FATAL -- but did not address the stack-cookie crash class; B-307 had the same silent-exit signature, 0xC0000409, per the prior smoke test description in `swarm_cpu_smoke.json`). The smoke harness `swarm_cpu_smoke` reproduces the silent exit class deterministically: pre-fix it crashes within ~1s of the 256 cycle with `exit code -1073740791` (= 0xC0000409); post-fix it cycles cleanly through 256 AND 512 with no abnormal exit. Fix: `roomGetProps` now honors `len`. The writelimit is `propnums + (len - 1)` (leaving one slot for the `-1` terminator). Once full, additional propnums are dropped (de-dup state remains valid via the existing in-buffer prefix walk), and a single `LOG_WARNING` fires per game frame (gated by `g_Vars.lvframe60`) so the log doesn't flood with the 256+ chr-tick callers all hitting the cap. Truncation is acceptable for the swarm scenario because swarm chrs run with `CHRHFLAG_PERIMDISABLED` (collision broadphase skips them) and the bot AI's target selection forces the player propnum directly -- the truncated rear-of-buffer chrs do not participate in any per-frame correctness path. For non-swarm scenes where a room legitimately holds >255 props (none known today), the truncation still beats the crash; bumping caller buffers to `>= MAX_PROPS` is the long-term scaling path. Companion change in `port/src/swarm_test.c`: `swarm_drain_death_state()` helper drains `ACT_DIE` / `ACT_DEAD` transient pointers (cover, target, fadealpha, act_die/act_dead notifychrindex) before chrRemove -- defensive cleanup for the case where the cycler force-frees chrs mid-death-animation (Mike's hypothesis from the triage; not the actual root cause but a hardening worth keeping). Net effect: `mainTick` log stops cold after `CHAT: Agent joined`, and the process hung until the smoke watchdog reaped it. Fix: skip the local slot at the loop head (`if (ncl == g_NetLocalClient) continue;`) plus a defensive `if (!ncl->peer) continue;` inside the state-gated branch. Dedicated servers have `g_NetLocalClient == NULL` so the guard is a no-op for that hosting mode. The listen host's own lobby state is already authoritative from `lobbyUpdate()` -- it doesn't need to receive its own SVC_LOBBY_LEADER. Companion: `netBroadcastRoomList` at `port/src/net/netmsg.c:7315` was already safe -- it uses `netSend(NULL, ...)` which routes through `enet_host_broadcast` (iterates ENet's peer list, which excludes the listen host's slot 0 because no peer was registered). Playtest verification: run `listen_host_peer_smoke.json` end-to-end and watch for `NET: broadcast SVC_LOBBY_LEADER: client N is leader` after `CHAT: Agent joined` in `pd-host.log`; the host's scripted exit at host-t=18s should now fire cleanly. Propagation check: same pattern (loop over `g_NetClients`, no local-slot skip, send via per-client peer) exists at `netmsg.c:7638` (CLC_ROOM_SETTINGS_UPDATE rebroadcast) and `netmsg.c:7709` (CLC_ROOM_PLAYLIST_UPDATE rebroadcast). Both filter by `room_id` first, so the listen-host slot is excluded in practice (host slot's `room_id = 0xFF` from netClientReset, won't match an active room). Spectator-frame loop at `netmsg.c:7011` filters by `CLFLAG_SPECTATOR`, also excluding the host slot. CLC_STAGE_READY at `netmsg.c:7377` filters by `CLSTATE_GAME` and breaks after the first match. No other immediate loop-with-netSend-to-per-client-peer hazards remain on the listen-server hot path. ---- ORIGINAL TRIAGE (2026-05-15, main-checkout-gpu-parity-and-wrap-up, c118 / connectivity): Orchestrated listen-host stops logging after `CHAT: Agent joined` when a real ENet peer attaches. The host's `mainTick` log path stops cold immediately after that line; the host's smoke-harness scripted-exit at host-t=18000ms does not fire (no `SMOKE: result=scripted_exit` in `pd-host.log`); the host is reaped by the runner's watchdog after `timeout_seconds + 30s`. Verified clean in single-process isolation: the SAME host binary with the SAME `--smoke` schedule runs cleanly to host-t=18s and emits the sentinel when NO client connects. The quirk only manifests when a real ENet peer attaches. Symptom is silent -- no FATAL, no EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, no smoke-result line. Suspect candidates: (a) `netBroadcastRoomList` SVC_ROOM_LIST send path on the listen-server side at `port/src/net/netmsg.c:7320` -- broadcasts after a peer joins to advertise the new room list; (b) listen-host `lobbyUpdate` leader-broadcast branch at `port/src/net/netmsg.c:836-847`, if `g_Lobby.leaderSlot` is not initialised correctly when `g_NetDedicated == 0` and the host is also the leader. Workaround: the `listen_host_peer_smoke.json` test was structured so all peer-link markers (`NET: incoming connection`, `NET: client slot N assigned to peer`) land BEFORE this point and the `SMOKE: result=scripted_exit` `required_counts` is `min: 1` (client only -- the client exits cleanly and proves the peer link succeeded end-to-end). | `port/src/net/netmsg.c` (likely 836-847 or 7320); `port/src/net/net.c` (lobby/leader state) | Reproduce: launch one client with `--host --listen-bind 27200`, separately launch another with `--connect-host 127.0.0.1:27200`, watch the host's `pd-host.log` -- last log line will be the `CHAT: Agent joined` after CLC_AUTH completes; subsequent host `mainTick` and netmsg log calls will not appear. | **B-323** | CRITICAL | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-05-03 (competent-saha-a202bb).** Mike's playtest of `dev 1363ee75` AVs at boot inside `challengesInit()`. Stack: `bcopy/memcpy+146` -> `dmaStart` -> `dmaExec` -> `dmaExecWithAutoAlign` -> `challengeLoadConfig` (`src/game/challenge.c:410` pre-fix) -> `challengeLoad` -> `challengesInit` -> `mainInit`. Last log line `VERBOSE: INIT: challengesInit...`, no breadcrumb (AV in first iteration). Root cause: PC-vs-N64 struct sizing drift. The mpconfigs ROM segment is 4576 bytes, mpstrings is 14080 bytes, both laid out using N64 binary struct sizes (mpstrings=320 bytes/entry). The PC port grew `MAX_BOTS` from 8 to 32, making `sizeof(struct mpconfig) = 0x11f4` (4596) and `sizeof(struct mpstrings) = 680`. Pre-Pass-C the over-read landed in adjacent ROM bytes inside the contiguous 32 MB g_RomFile blob -- harmless. Post-Pass-C (S607, dev `b15cc701`, 2026-05-02) each segment is its own heap allocation with 64 bytes of read-ahead padding; the over-read walks off the end and AVs. `g_MpChallenges[0].confignum = MPCONFIG_CHALLENGE01 = 14` so the very first call attempts to read 4596 bytes from segment offset `14 * 4596 = 64344` -- ~60 KB past the segment end. Fix: (1) Remove the mpconfigs `dmaExec` -- the data was always overwritten by `mpconfig->config = g_MpConfigs[confignum]`, so the read was dead code. The buffer is now aligned via `ALIGN16((uintptr_t)buffer)` directly. (2) Replace the mpstrings `dmaExec` with `bcopy` of `N64_MPSTRINGS_SIZE = 320` bytes from offset `confignum * 320` into the head of the PC mpstrings struct (description[200] + aibotnames[0..7] = 320 bytes -- matches N64 layout exactly), with `bzero` of the whole PC struct first to leave aibotnames[8..31] zeroed. Bots 9..32 fall back to legacy `g_BotConfigsArray` naming when no segment-sourced name is supplied. Confignum range [0, 43]: `43 * 320 + 320 = 14080` exactly the segment size, within bounds for every legal value. Propagation check: other `dmaExecWithAutoAlign` callers (`anim.c::animsInit`, `training.c::frLoadRomData`, both via `_animationsTableRomStart` / `_firingrangeSegmentRomStart`) use caller-supplied lengths bounded by the actual segment size (not PC-grown struct sizeof), so the AV class is bounded to `challengeLoadConfig`. The mpconfigs segment is now structurally unused; future cleanup can retire it from `port/src/romdata.c::ROMSEG_LIST` if desired. | `src/game/challenge.c` | Build verify: queued `build-session.ps1 -Session b323 -Target all/server/tests` PASS (client 55.5 MB, updater 12.3 MB, server 22.4 MB, tests 24.6 MB). | **B-313** | CRITICAL | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-05-03 (S607, catalog-slice12-passc, dev `6f9a4a84`).** Mike's playtest of the B-306 fix unblocked door modeldef loads but exposed a third Pass C regression: `0xc0000005` in `memcpy+146` called from `challengeLoadConfig+0x12a -> dmaExecWithAutoAlign+0x43 -> dmaExec+0xf -> dmaStart+0x15 -> bcopy+0x12`.  Boot stack: `mainInit -> challengesInit -> challengeLoad -> challengeLoadConfig -> dmaExecWithAutoAlign(buffer, _mpconfigsSegmentRomStart + confignum * sizeof(struct mpconfig), sizeof(struct mpconfig))`.  Root cause: `dmaExecWithAutoAlign` (`src/lib/dma.c:115`) rounds the read length up via `ALIGN16`, so a `sizeof(struct mpconfig) = 0x11f4` (4596) request becomes a `0x1200` (4608) memcpy.  The `mpconfigs` segment is only `0x11e0` (4576) bytes, so the consumer over-reads by 32 bytes.  Pre-Pass-C this was harmless because the segment lived inside g_RomFile (a contiguous 32 MB blob) and the over-read landed inside the next segment's bytes.  Post-Pass-C `romdataReleaseRom` reloaded each `SRC_ROM` segment from disk via `fsFileLoad`, which only allocates `size + 1` bytes.  The +1 byte was insufficient and the over-read walked into unmapped memory.  Same hazard applies to every `dmaExec`/`dmaExecWithAutoAlign` consumer that reads from a migrated segment with `ALIGN16`-rounded or struct-sized lengths: `mpstringsX` (`challenge.c`), `fontjpnsingle`/`fontjpnmulti` (`lang.c`), `textureslist` (`texinit.c`), `firingrange` (`training.c`), `_animationsTableRomStart` (`anim.c::animsInit`).  All assume "ROM is one contiguous blob" semantics.  Fix: when migrating segments to disk-backed heap, allocate via `sysMemAlloc(diskSize + PASSC_SEG_PADDING)` with `PASSC_SEG_PADDING = 0x40` bytes of zero-initialised read-ahead slack, using raw `fopen`+`fread` instead of `fsFileLoad` so the padding is explicit.  64 bytes covers `ALIGN16` (15 max) plus struct-size over-reads (mpconfig is the worst case at 20).  Other migration paths unaffected: `segNormalised` (preprocess returned heap, e.g. `preprocessFont`/`preprocessALBankFile`) keeps its own buffer sized by the preprocess function; consumers don't over-read those buffers because they were always heap-backed pre-Pass-C and proven against heap-overread. | `port/src/romdata.c` | Build verify: queued `build-session.ps1 -Session passc-fix4 -Target client` PASS (CLIENT 24s, PerfectDark.exe 54.8 MB). Grep `pd-client.log` for `FATAL`/`ACCESS_VIOLATION` between `ROMRELEASE` and the title screen: zero hits expected.  If the next crash hits a `dmaExec`-style segment over-read site I missed, raise `PASSC_SEG_PADDING` -- the worst-case struct-size over-read that ships in the codebase is `sizeof(struct mpconfig) - 0x11e0 = 0x14`, well under 0x40. |

The GPU pipeline still caps at SWARM_GPU_MAX=256 SSBO size which is a separate scaling concern (B-308/B-309/B-310). After migrating any segment, if the segment is named `"animations"` recompute the externs to point at the new heap buffer (same offset within `seg->size`). Audit confirmed no other preprocess publishes ROM-relative externs (`preprocessFont` / `preprocessALBankFile` already return heap; `preprocessSequences` / `preprocessJpnFont` / `preprocessTexturesList` / `preprocessMpConfigs` / `preprocessALCMidiHdr` only byteswap in place without setting externs). `ROMRELEASE` log line gains a `names migrated=N` count. The system self-corrects later when the catalog populates and `modmgrEnsureCaches` rebuilds; gameplay-time consumers see the right counts. Documented gap (forgemode.c:78 comment, untouched until now): "full engine-level model hot-reload requires additional plumbing (bodyAllocateModel for the new pair) which is currently logged-only". Log evidence: `forgeTransitionToFreefly haschrbody=0 handmodeldef=NULL` AND `forgeTransitionToNormal haschrbody=0 handmodeldef=NULL` for the entire 3+ minute Grid session despite the body-swap-save log line firing at FREEFLY entry. Root cause: prior code only twiddled `chr->bodynum` / `chr->headnum` integer fields and trusted "the legacy model-reload pipeline picks up the change on the next per-chr model tick" -- empirically false. `chr->model` stayed at its allocation-time value (NULL when the player's chr was created on Grid stage entry because forge intercepted before TICKMODE_CUTSCENE / MPSWIRL could populate it). Fix: extend `forge_freefly_state_t` with `saved_chrmodel` + `has_saved_chrmodel`. `forgeSetFreeflyMode` now calls `bodyAllocateModel(BODY_DRCAROLL, HEAD_RANDOM_GENDER, 0)` after the bodynum/headnum write and assigns the result to `chr->model`; for player 0 also flips `p->haschrbody=true` and `p->model00d4=newmodel`. `forgeRestorePlayerMode` restores the saved chr->model pointer (gunmem/modelmgr-owned Agent allocation) plus the integer fields; if the saved pointer was NULL (forge intercepted before playerTickChrBody had populated it) it allocates a fresh Agent body via bodyAllocateModel as a fallback. Bounded leak: the Dr Carroll model we allocate at FREEFLY entry is not explicitly freed -- per-transition slot release would require deeper modelmgr/gunmem plumbing; memory growth bounded to one alloc per FREEFLY entry, reclaimed at next stage unload. | **B-295** | HIGH | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-05-01 (S593g follow-up #5: integrated-head warning gate in body.c).** Mike's 2026-05-01 playtest log captured 550 `WARNING: CHR.DIAG: bodyAllocateModel head_canon=NULL for headnum=0` lines firing in waves at each swarm-cycle change (4 -> 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 48 -> 64 -> 128 -> 256 = 556 bot allocations across the full ladder). Skedar (body 92) is an integrated-head body -- `catalogGetBodyIsComplete` returns true, the head geometry is part of the body model, the headnum slot is unused by the body alloc path. The warning at `body.c:405` was firing unconditionally for any `headnum >= 0 && head_canon == NULL` combination regardless of body type, so the swarm scenario filled the log with structurally-meaningless misses. Log file ended abruptly at 02:10.72 mid-spawn-flood -- 256 fopen/fwrite/fclose log calls in one frame (one warning per Skedar spawn) was a plausible contributor (file-flush stall under spawn pressure). **Fix**: extend the warning gate to `!catalogGetBodyIsComplete(bodynum)` in body.c. The warning still fires for separate-head bodies where a missing catalog head IS a real load-time problem; integrated-head bodies skip cleanly. **PRIOR S593f FIX still in place**: S593e's visual half-scale fix didn't touch the chr collision geometry (`chr->radius` / `chr->height`). Mike's playtest confirmed: "I think the tiny skedar still had regular sized colliders." With 256 chrs spawned at a single radius=600 ring, per-chr arc length was 14.7 vs 30-unit collision footprint -- every chr fully overlapped its neighbours, the per-chr push-resolution loop in `chrCalculatePushPos` could not find a clear push direction, and the bots froze in place exactly where they spawned (Mike's "256 wave didn't apply movement at all"). The crash that followed at 256 was likely a downstream consequence. **Fix**: (1) `chr->radius = 15` (half of 30) and `chr->height = 92` (half of chrInit default 185) at swarm spawn, matching the half visual scale; (2) multi-ring spawn distribution: SWARM_PER_RING=24 chrs per ring, ring step 200u, base 600u. At 256 chrs that's 11 rings reaching out to ~2600u with per-chr arc spacing always larger than the chr footprint. **PRIOR S593e FIX still in place**: S593d gave swarm bots hostile teams + aggressive AI + scale/health/speed + Debug Menu UX, but Mike's playtest found three remaining issues, two with a shared root cause. **Issue A (huge bots)**: `modelSetScale(chr->model, 0.5f)` directly REPLACED model->scale with 0.5, but `model->scale` is a multiplier on `model->definition->scale` which is ~1000 for chr bodies, and `bodyAllocateModel` initialises model->scale to a small value (~0.07 for Skedar via `scaleRaw * 0.1` in body.c:204 plus per-body height variation). Setting it to 0.5 produced ~7x natural size -> bots clipped into walls / ceilings on Car Park / Felicity. Fix: multiply by 0.5 (`chr->model->scale * 0.5f`) instead of replacing, preserving body-specific scaling. **Issue B (crash on 256 -> wrap to 4)**: playtest log showed repeated "WARNING: MODELMGR: All rwdata binding pools exhausted (type3=64) for rwdatalen=330 - heap fallback" starting at cycle 128. Skedar bodies have rwdatalen=330 words (Type 3 territory), NUMTYPE3 was 64. Over-cap chrs fell through to mempAlloc which is NOT freed by chrRemove -> heap-fallback chunks leak across cycles, exhausting MEMPOOL_STAGE after cycling 256 -> 4 -> 256 a few times -> next allocate crashes. Fix: bump NUMTYPE3 64 -> 320 in `modelmgr.c` + `modelmgrreset.c` (KEEP IN SYNC). Cost ~492 KB rwdata, acceptable. **Issue C (arena selector mismatch)**: playtest log showed `failed to resolve map_id='base:arena_mp_carpark'` with fallback to Felicity. The Debug Menu arena selector was passing `base:arena_*` (catalog ARENA id) but `testScenarioLaunch::resolve_map_stagenum` calls `catalogResolveStage` which matches `base:mp_*` (catalog STAGE id). Fix: at arena collect time, convert via `catalogStageIdByStagenum(arena_entry.stagenum)` so the selector stores stage ids that resolve. **PRIOR S593d FIX still in place**: S593c brought CPU bots up to real-bot ticks, but Mike's playtest found them "running aimlessly" -- the smoking gun was `chr->team = 1 << 7 = TEAM_NONCOMBAT (0x80)`. The engine's team taxonomy treats TEAM_NONCOMBAT as a "do not engage" signal, so bots had AI ticks but the hostility check classified them as non-combatants. Fix: dedicated swarm bot config (`s_SwarmBotConfig`: `BOTTYPE_KAZE` + `BOTDIFF_PERFECT`), `chr->team = TEAM_ENEMY` (different from player's TEAM_01), `aibot->command = AIBOTCMD_ATTACK` with `attackpropnum` = player. Half-scale via `modelSetScale(chr->model, 0.5f)`, half-health (`chr->maxdamage = 4.0`), 1.5x speed (PERFECT difficulty for CPU bots ~1.47x; max_speed 18 -> 27 for GPU compute path and gpu_fallback_seek_tick). Default arena changed from `base:mp_skedar` (cramped) to `base:mp_felicity` (open beach). Debug Menu UX redesigned: 3 radio modes (The Grid / CPU Bots / GPU Bots) + catalog-enumerated arena selector (`ASSET_ARENA`) + Start button. Team highlights suppressed naturally because `MPOPTION_TEAMSENABLED` is unset in our test scenario's `g_MpSetup.options`. GPU full-bot-AI remains the documented follow-up at [designs/in-flight/gpu-swarm-bot-pipeline.md](designs/in-flight/gpu-swarm-bot-pipeline.md). **PRIOR S593c FIX still in place**: First-pass S593 fix (2026-04-30) addressed the AV at PC `0x3ab39f` and a model-pool ceiling, but Mike's playtest revealed three remaining symptoms: cycler stuck at 8, Skedars moved as props with no real bot AI (CPU+GPU), no chr-vs-chr / chr-vs-player collision. **Cycler-stuck root cause**: `setup.c::chrmgrConfigure` was missing the same `testScenarioGetSwarmMaxCount()` swarm hook that `modelmgrAllocateSlots` already had. With `numchrs = PLAYERCOUNT() + 0 + 10` on a solo-no-simulants swarm session, `g_NumChrSlots = 11`, so the chr pool ran out after the player + ~10 chrs. Fix: mirror the swarm hook in the chrmgr path. **No-bot-AI / no-collision root cause**: swarm chrs were spawned with `ailist=GAILIST_IDLE` and no `aibot` -- they were ticking through `chraTick`'s passive paths only, no target acquisition, no movement intent, no collision-aware step. `chrSetPos` direct writes covered the visible-motion gap but bypassed the bot-ai-driven movement that handles chr-vs-chr collision via `chrTryStop`. Fix: CPU mode now spawns each chr as a real bot (`ailist=GAILIST_AIBOT_INIT`, `chr->myaction=MA_AIBOTMAINLOOP`, `botinvInit`), with `chr->aibot` pointing into a private 256-slot aibot pool that escapes the `MAX_BOTS=32` cap of `botmgrAllocateBot` while skipping its match-scoring registrations (`g_MpBotChrPtrs` etc.) that overflow at MAX_MPCHRS=40. CPU bots now seek/attack/dodge with collision. `chr->radius=30` is set so the perim has a meaningful size for the collision system. **GPU mode** keeps the position-only behaviour with `gpu_fallback_seek_tick` when compute is unavailable; full bot behaviour on GPU is filed as a follow-up pillar (`context/designs/in-flight/gpu-swarm-bot-pipeline.md`) since the gap is large (new compute kernel, AI state on GPU, GPU-side LOS/target acquisition). **First-pass fixes (S593, 2026-04-30) still in place**: `despawn_all` uses the canonical chrmgrStop pattern (`chrRemove + propDelist + propDisable + propFree`); `chrTick` early-outs with `TICKOP_FREE` + `CHR.STALE.MISS:` warning when `chr == NULL || chr->chrnum < 0 || chr->model == NULL`; NUMTYPE1/2/3 bumped 80/320/64 so 256 chrs fit in the rwdata binding pool; `apply_player_setup()` re-asserts invincibility / all-guns / bottomless ammo every tick; cycle ladder 4/8/16/32/48/64/128/256. | `port/src/swarm_test.c`; `port/fast3d/swarm_gpu.cpp`; `port/src/testscenarios.c`; `port/fast3d/pdgui_menu_mainmenu.cpp` (S593d, 2026-05-01); `src/game/setup.c`; `context/designs/in-flight/gpu-swarm-bot-pipeline.md` (S593c, 2026-05-01); `port/include/swarm_test.h`; `src/game/chr.c`; `src/game/modelmgr.c`; `src/game/modelmgrreset.c` (S593, 2026-04-30) | Manual playtest: Settings -> Debug -> Test Scenarios. Default mode = CPU Bots, default arena = Felicity. Click Start. Verify: cycler reaches 256 (4->8->16->32->48->64->128->256->4 via D-pad-Down or [0]); Skedars are half-size, chase + fire on the player aggressively, do not pass through each other or the player; switching mode to GPU Bots and a different arena via the selector launches that arena (GPU bots are position-only per `gpu-swarm-bot-pipeline.md`). Log invariants: `CHRSLOTS: added 256 swarm chr slots for benchmark` at level load; no `CHR.STALE.MISS:` warnings; no `0xc0000005` exception. |

Clients route the packet to audioMusicSyncReceive (audio.c) which on a track-change starts the new track and hard-seeks to the host offset (late-joiners pick up mid-song), and on a same-track receive caches the (recv_wallclock, host_offset_at_recv) pair for the correction tick. audioMusicSyncCorrectionTick runs once per audio frame from the end of audioEndFrame: it computes drift = expected_host_offset_now - local_position_ms, then either holds rate at 1.0 (drift inside +-30 ms dead-band), lerps rate via clamp(1.0 + drift_ms*0.001, 0.97, 1.03) for moderate drift, or hard-seeks to the host offset when drift exceeds +-5000 ms. modmusic backend rewrote the integer-cursor mix loop to use a fractional cursor with linear interpolation between adjacent stereo frames so sub-sample rate changes work cleanly; rate is reset to 1.0 on every modMusicPlay / Stop. New API: modMusicSetRate / GetRate, modMusicGetPositionMs / SetPositionMs, modMusicGetDurationMs. Diagnostic: throttled "MUSIC.SYNC: drift=N ms rate=X.XX" log every 2 s when actively correcting, plus "MUSIC.SYNC: hard-seek..." when the band is exceeded. | `port/include/net/net.h` (NET_PROTOCOL_VER 40 + comment), `port/src/net/netmsg.c` (SVC_MUSIC_ADVANCE write/read + broadcast), `port/include/net/netmsg.h` (signature change), `port/src/audio.c` (host re-broadcast tick + audioMusicSyncReceive + audioMusicSyncCorrectionTick), `port/src/modmusic.c` (fractional-cursor mix loop + rate/position API), `port/include/modmusic.h` (new API), `port/include/audio.h` (sync entry points), `port/src/server_stubs.c` (no-op stubs for pd-server) | **Playtest:** (1) Two listen-host clients in the same MP match: start a track on the host, observe both hear the track; check logs for "MUSIC.SYNC: drift=... rate=..." lines stabilising near rate=1.0. (2) Start a fresh client mid-track: track starts at the host's current offset, not from the beginning; check log for "MUSIC.SYNC: track-change -> '...' offset=N ms". (3) Force drift on the client (e.g. simulate a hitch via Audio.QueueLimit, or temporarily rate-disable the host re-broadcast): drift should exceed 5000 ms and the client should hard-seek -- log "MUSIC.SYNC: hard-seek (drift=... exceeded)". (4) Pitch shift at +-3% rate: audible if listening for it but transient -- the lerp deadband of +-30 ms and gain K=0.001 means rates only push toward the boundaries during sustained drift. |

| **B-199** | CRITICAL | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-04-19 (happy-blackburn-8eb2ff)**. `0xc0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION` crashing the game 80 ms after loading Investigation (stagenum `0x33`, bgfile 31 `bg_ear.seg`). addr2line stack: `func0f00505c dlights.c:1836 → func0f004c6c dlights.c:1787 → lightsReset dlights.c:561 → lvReset lv.c:615 → mainLoop pdmain.c:594`. Crash at `var8006142c[portalnum2][portalnum]` with out-of-range `portalnum2` read from a garbage `g_RoomPortals[]` entry. Root cause: the B-185 safety in `bgLoadFile` (fbc276ce) used a single `memset(memaddr, 0, len)` on any `len > romsize - offset` condition — which fires for every call whose `len` is rounded up to 16-byte alignment even when the final 1–15 bytes are just off-file padding. Investigation's `bg_ear.seg` section 3 is 1254 bytes at offset 195850 but the aligned read length is 1264 (`((section3compsize-1)|0xf)+1`); file ends at 197104, so `offset+len` overshoots by exactly 10 bytes. The aggressive `memset` destroyed all 1254 valid bytes of the compressed portal blob, `bgInflate` then produced zeroes, and `g_Rooms[]` / `g_RoomPortals[]` came back with invalid portal indices. Triggered specifically on Investigation because `bg_ear.seg` section 3 is not 16-byte-padded in the ROM; other stages happened to be aligned. Pre-existing latent since B-185 (01:35, 2026-04-19); surfaced during Wave 1 Super Audit playtest when user loaded Investigation. Fix: `bgLoadFile` split into three paths — (1) `offset >= romsize` → zero all (offset past EOF, no valid data); (2) `len > romsize - offset` → partial read — `memcpy(memaddr, src+offset, romsize-offset)` then zero only the padding bytes; only log an ERROR when the missing bytes exceed 16 (alignment gap is silent, real corruption still logs); (3) else → full memcpy. Preserves B-185's deterministic-zero intent for true failure modes while letting aligned reads succeed with their real data. Build clean 2/2 (PerfectDark + PerfectDarkServer). | `src/game/bg.c` | Load Combat Sim → **Investigation** (stagenum 0x33). Stage should load without crashing in `func0f00505c`. No `BG.LOAD: partial over-read` ERROR should appear for Investigation's section 3 load (the 10-byte gap is alignment padding ≤ 16, below the warn threshold). Regression check: load Complex, Skedar Ruins, Villa, Temple, Sewers, Crashsite — every stage should still load correctly (aligned sections follow the full-`memcpy` path). If any stage logs `BG.LOAD: partial over-read ... copied=N` with a gap > 16 bytes, that's real data corruption in the seg file and needs separate triage. |

Build version `dev f32d1e51`. Root cause: Complex room 7's inflated gfx data was 576 bytes (printed `size 1152` is the internal post-doubled scratch size) and the PC-port 32→64-bit preprocessing produced 15528 bytes of output — a ~27× expansion that far exceeds the 2× scratch multiplier hardcoded in `preprocessBgRoom`. The legitimate per-room 64-bit pointer expansion is ~2×, so the runaway output was reads past the end of the per-room inflated buffer: on N64 the whole BG segment was a single contiguous blob so `roomblock.ptr_gdl` / `ptr_vertices` / `ptr_colours` could reference offsets anywhere in the segment; in the PC port each room is inflated into its own independent buffer by `bgInflate`, so any offset pointing past this room's data walks into adjacent garbage. `gbiConvertGdl` (port/src/preprocess/gbi.c) read until it found a byte matching `G_ENDDL` (0xB8) and wrote 2× (8 → 16 bytes/cmd) of host output for every read — ~485 bogus commands = 7764 src bytes read, 15528 dst bytes written — blowing the scratch and the caller's allocation. Three-layer fix: (1) `gbiConvertGdl` now takes an explicit `src_size` and synthesizes an ENDDL when a read would cross that boundary (logged `WARNING: gbiConvertGdl: source overrun at srcpos=… src_size=…`). (2) `convertRoomGfxData` clamps `endpos` / `vtx_end` / `col_end` to the actual inflated `src_size` and skips any `ptr_gdl` whose offset is outside the buffer (logged `WARNING: convertRoomGfxData: gdl[i] src_offset=… outside src_size=… — skipping`). (3) `preprocessBgRoom` bumps the scratch dst allocation from 2× → 8× with a 4 KB floor; `sysFatalError` replaced with `LOG_ERROR` + `return 0` so a malformed room degrades rather than killing the process. `src/game/bg.c`'s caller allocation bumped from 2× → 8× with a 16 KB floor so the `memcpy(data, dst, newSize)` back into the allocation cannot overflow. Caller guard added: `if (inflatedlen == 0)` skips room load cleanly. Callers `filemodel.c:660` updated to pass `src_file_len`. `port/src/preprocess/gbi.c` now includes `system.h` for `sysLogPrintf`. | `port/include/preprocess/gbi.h`, `port/src/preprocess/gbi.c`, `port/src/preprocess/filebg.c`, `port/src/preprocess/filemodel.c`, `src/game/bg.c` | Boot build, play Combat Sim → Complex (solo, 1 player, 0 bots). Stage must load and render all 45 rooms without the `FATAL: overflow when trying to preprocess a bg room` crash. Log may include `WARNING: convertRoomGfxData: gdl[i] src_offset=… outside src_size=…` or `WARNING: gbiConvertGdl: source overrun at srcpos=… src_size=…` for the specific room(s) whose ROM data referenced cross-room GDL offsets — those rooms may render with minor visual glitches (missing a GDL) but the game stays alive. Repeat on other stages (Temple, Ravine, G5 Building, Skedar Ruins) to regression-check stage loading. |

| **B-193** | HIGH | **ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED + FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-04-19 (elated-hugle-7ec221 — S384)**. Commit `fe107e3e` (2026-04-17, M4 optimisation) collapsed `ALIGN16(val)` to `(val)` on the grounds that `mempAlloc` already returns aligned memory. That rationale held for SIZE-only uses but not for POINTER uses — `bg.c:1516` / `bg.c:1934` do `header = (u8 *)ALIGN16((uintptr_t)headerbuffer)` where `headerbuffer` is a `u8[0x50]` stack buffer that's meant to be advanced to a 16-aligned start before `preprocessBgSection{1,2,3}Header` parses structured fields out of it. With the no-op macro the parse runs from whatever offset the stack gave — on 64-bit the stack is usually 16-aligned so it MAY work (explaining the intermittent reproduction and the "not reproducing after a clean rebuild" brave-bouman observation on 5 cold boots — rebuilds shift stack frame layouts), but nothing guarantees it, and any function above in the call tree with misaligned locals shifts `headerbuffer` off. Identical unpatched pointer use at `bg.c:1537` (`scratch` inflate-buffer pointer) corrupts the primary-data buffer whenever the shift crosses a 16-byte lane. **Fix**: restore `ALIGN16(val)` to `((((val) + 0xf) | 0xf) ^ 0xf)` in `src/include/constants.h:79` so every pointer-alignment site gets a real round-up. 0–15 bytes of padding per allocation is trivial overhead on modern hardware. Build clean 777/777. `PerfectDark.exe` 53,232,611 / `PerfectDarkServer.exe` 23,154,674. But was NOT sufficient to fix the stage 0x26 torn-models symptom; see B-166 for the over-aggressive guard that was the actual cause of the user-visible symptom. This is the true root cause of B-161's "WHY models load torn in stage 0x26" open question. Repro: dev build `34636b53`, 64 MB memp, title loads OK, enter CI Training (0x26) from main menu — every body/head/prop in `MANIFEST-SP: applied diff — load=56 unload=0 keep=3` comes back torn (`MODELDEF: file N loaded torn — parts=0`). S323's `modeldefLoad` reject + S317/S327/S358 call-site guards correctly converted the AV into WARNING log lines, but the underlying load was still corrupted. Root cause: `src/game/file.c::fileLoadRomToNew` gated `info->loadedsize` recomputation on `loadedsize == 0`, but `fileLoad` overwrites `info->loadedsize` with the post-preprocess size on exit — stripping the `+0x8000` rzipInflate scratch buffer. On re-entry, `mempAlloc(info->loadedsize, MEMPOOL_STAGE)` allocates only the post-preprocess size; inside `fileLoad`, `scratch = dst + allocationlen - aligned(romsize)` falls inside the dst buffer. In-place inflate corrupts the deflate stream as the writer catches the reader → `rzipInflate` returns 0 → `romdataFilePreprocess` skips on `size==0` → dst stays zeroed → `modeldef->numparts=0`, `rootnode=NULL`, "loaded torn". Trigger chain: `catalogValidateAll()` at startup pre-loads every body/head through `safeModeldefLoad → modeldefLoadToNew → fileLoadRomToNew` (populates `loadedsize` for 151+ files), title stage uses `fileLoadToAddr` (resets `loadedsize=0` each call — immune), `mempResetPool(STAGE)` wipes allocations on CI transition but leaves `g_FileInfo[]` intact, CI manifest re-loads the same bodies/heads via `modeldefLoadToNew` → hits stale cache path → corruption. Fix: drop the `loadedsize==0` gate entirely; always recompute. Correctness for both EXTRAMEM and DEFAULT in one stroke. Cost: one extra `fileGetInflatedSize` (0x40-byte DMA + rzip header check) on cached loads — sub-ms at stage-transition time. Commits `e1205034` (Option A gated fix) → `b88df691` (gate removed, final). Merged `2e4f07d6`. Build clean 780/780 then 2/2 incremental. | `src/game/file.c:257` | Cold boot → main menu → CI Training (0x26). Root cause: `actionmapPollFrame()` WASD→AXIS_MOVE synthesis block only writes `s_State[0][ACTION_AXIS_MOVE_X/Y].value` when at least one WASD key is held. When no controller is enumerated on player 0 (keyboard-only setup, or controller not plugged in for P0 slot), the controller-polling branch at line 803 is skipped, so nothing else resets `.value` each frame. After the user presses and releases W, the synthesis wrote `.value=1.0` during press; on release the block short-circuited (`mx=my=0`) and `.value` stayed at 1.0. The feedback loop: next frame reads stale `.value=1.0`, sets `analogStickActive=true`, skips synthesis — axis pegged forever. Menu open clears AXIS_MOVE via the `menuActive` branch at line 860, hence the "reopen fixes it" symptom. Fix: (a) track `p0CtrlDroveAxis` — true only when the controller actually wrote AXIS_MOVE this frame — and gate `analogStickActive` on it, so stale `.value` never suppresses the synthesis; (b) always assign the computed `mx/my` (including zero) when `!analogStickActive`, so WASD release writes `.value=0.0` and clears the stuck axis. | `port/src/actionmap.cpp` | Playtest: keyboard-only; open main menu → close → press+release W, A, S, D individually. Root cause identified: original N64 amgrFrame brake threshold of **1100 stereo samples = 50ms cushion** was smaller than typical PC main-thread hitches (50–100ms), so queue drained below the 128-sample SDL underrun threshold routinely. Producer/consumer math at 22050 Hz stereo × 60 Hz NTSC is 368 vs 367.5 stereo samples/frame = net +0.5/frame drift, so from a cold queue it took ~36 seconds to reach the 1100 target — meaning startup + hitch-recovery were both slow. **Fix**: three-tier production pacing in `src/lib/audiomgr.c::amgrFrame`. (tier 1) queue > **3000** → push 184 brake. (tier 2) queue 2500–3000 → push 368 steady (legacy drift rate). (tier 3) queue < 2500 → push **736** fast-fill (4 naudio chunks of 184; fits in the 3072-byte info->data allocation). Steady state now oscillates 2800–3000 (~128–136ms cushion, 3× original). Cold fill to 2500 takes 7 frames (~115ms) instead of 36 seconds. PAL retains its 552/frame rate (already sufficient for 50Hz). | `src/lib/audiomgr.c` | Playtest: play any arena for 60s, tail `pd-client.log` for `AUDIO[B-141]: 30s summary` lines. Expect `underruns=0` steady state; any residual underruns correlate with actual main-loop stalls > 135ms. `nullProducer` count should stay zero if `sndInit` ran. `buffered(samples) min` should now hover 2800–3000 instead of 900–1100. |

Next repro should produce enough log evidence on the first frame to pick which of the six hypotheses fired.
- **Bug D (invisible networked bots on Chicago)** — bots visible on minimap and audible but not rendered in world. Likely chr generation token mismatch (FIX-A.2 area); may have cleared with recent drops. **Instrumented S301 (confident-chaum)**: `CHR.DIAG:` prefix on three points — `botmgrAllocateBot` logs chrnum / body / head / body_id / head_id at entry and the returned model ptr (with WARNING if NULL), `bodyAllocateModel` logs body_canon / head_canon lookups (WARNING if catalog ID is NULL for a non-negative bodynum/headnum), `botSpawn` before (`BOT.SPAWN` breadcrumb + `CHR.DIAG: botSpawn …`) and after (`CHR.DIAG: botSpawn DONE …`) with the full invisible-state check: `WARNING chrnum=… is INVISIBLE after botSpawn (model=NULL|HIDDEN|VOID(-1))`. An invisible bot now leaves an explicit fingerprint identifying which field was the cause.
- **Chicago silent crash ~9 s** — needs VEH log + symbolify. **Instrumented S301 (confident-chaum)**: new `port/src/crashbreadcrumb.c` ring buffer (256 slots × 112 bytes, static BSS) dumped by VEH / UEF / SIGABRT / Linux `sigaction` paths directly into `pd.crash.log` / `pd.log` / `pd-client.log` under a `CRASH.DIAG: breadcrumb ring dump follows:` heading. Push sites: mainTick heartbeat per frame, lvTick per frame, chraTickBg per frame, chraTick per chr (slot + action + race), bwalkTick per player (pos + room + floorroom), botSpawn, botmgrAllocateBot, mainChangeToStage, SVC_STAGE_START send/receive. Ring holds ~130 ms of CHR.TICK pushes (32 bots × 60 Hz = 1920/s), enough to identify which chr + action was being ticked at the moment of crash. No dependency on ordinary log output — even a crash that corrupts sysLogPrintf will still dump the ring.
- **Airbase Start-Match 0xc0000005 / no-response** — log shows manifest OK but no SVC_STAGE_START. May share root cause with Bug A (fix shipped `d37e9677`). **Instrumented S301 (confident-chaum)**: `MATCHSTART.DIAG:` tag on every decision point in the match-start chain — `matchStart` entry / pre-mpStartMatch / post-mpStartMatch, `netServerStageStart` entry + send outcome (`SVC_STAGE_START sent to room 0x… (combat sim)` or `…broadcast to all clients`), `netmsgSvcStageStartWrite` begin, `netmsgSvcStageStartRead` begin. Each bail has an explicit reason message (`BAILED reason=empty_stage_id`, `SVC_STAGE reject — client state=… not in LOBBY/GAME/PREPARING`). With both sides tagged, one Airbase repro is enough to pin the decision point that stopped progress.

| **B-179** | HIGH | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-04-19 (sweet-chandrasekhar-7d64da — S371)**. 22/32 bots defaulting to mphead=0 (Joanna Dark head) in MP. Six specific heads load with parts=0 (torn modeldefs): `head_dark_snow`, `head_ddshock`, `head_carrington`, `head_ddsniper`, `head_president`, `head_cassandra`. Root cause: `validateModeldef` in `port/src/modelcatalog.c` was the remaining `numparts <= 0 ⟹ INVALID` guard that B-166 (`modeldefLoad`) and B-167 (`propobj.c` bbox walkers) did not propagate to. When a head's modeldef had parts=0 but valid rootnode/skel (the six heads above), the catalog marked it INVALID, and every `catalogValidateHeadId()` call (SVC_STAGE_START read paths in `netmsg.c:1366/1421/4792`) fell back through `catalogGetSafeHead → CATALOG_FALLBACK_HEAD` to head 0 (dark_combat = Joanna Dark). 22 of 32 bots either picked one of those six heads directly or had their default paired head routed through this fallback. Fix: `validateModeldef` now only rejects `numparts <= 0` when `category == MODELCAT_BODY` (bodies need skeletal parts for `body0f02ce8c` merge; falling back to dark_combat is the correct UX for torn bodies). Heads pass through with parts=0 — rendering walks rootnode DL nodes, `modelAttachHead` only needs rootnode, `modelGetPart` already returns NULL on parts=0 and every caller tolerates that (sunglasses/hudpiece toggles simply skipped). Build clean 774/774. `PerfectDark.exe` 53,202,559 / `PerfectDarkServer.exe` 23,141,856. | `port/src/modelcatalog.c` | Playtest: MP Combat Sim with 30+ bots — bots should wear their actual assigned heads (Cassandra, President, Carrington, DD-variants, Dark Snow) rather than 22 identical Joanna Dark heads. `CATALOG: [idx] file 0x%04x — numparts=0 out of range (INVALID)` warnings at validation time should disappear for the six head filenums. |
| **B-180** | HIGH | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-04-19 (cascade of B-179 — S371)**. Missing necks on all character models. Cascades from B-179: when 22/32 bots were being downgraded to the Joanna Dark head, the head-to-body fit was wrong and neck geometry (part of each head's own rootnode mesh) appeared missing or mismatched. With B-179 fix installed, each bot now loads its actual head (including neck geometry) and attaches via `modelAttachHead` to the body's headspot. `bodyCalculateHeadOffset` still runs for cross-gender/cross-type pairings to realign the head vertically. | `port/src/modelcatalog.c` (cascade fix) | Playtest: after B-179 playtest passes, verify each bot has a visible neck connecting head to body — no floating heads, no disconnected meshes. |
| **B-181** | MED | **FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-04-19 (interesting-nobel-184c6c)**. Wrong weapons spawning in match — map has 10 weapon markers vs target 16, fallback path was injecting unexpected weapons outside the selected weapon set. Root cause: `setupCreateProps` fallback (`src/game/setup.c:2467`, added in commit `0b62fc68` to force spawn-with-weapon when world pickups < desiredPickups) used `catalogIdByRuntime(ASSET_WEAPON, g_MpSetup.weapons[i])` to look up a catalog ID from an MPWEAPON_* index — but the runtime cache for ASSET_WEAPON is indexed by catalog *array position* (`e->runtime_index = i` in `assetcatalog_base_extended.c`, not by weapon_id), so MPWEAPON_FALCON2 (0x01) resolved to `"base:falcon2_silencer"` (MPWEAPON_FALCON2_SILENCER at array position 1). Additional issue: the fallback set `spawn_weapon_id` but never re-derived `spawnWeaponNum` (matchStart already ran), so the current match continued to use the pre-fallback spawn weapon, and the wrong ID persisted into the NEXT match when matchStart re-read it. Fix: replaced the `catalogIdByRuntime` lookup with a catalog scan that matches `ext.weapon.weapon_id == mpw` (same pattern as `savefile.c:816` and `buildSpawnWeaponList`). Skip MPWEAPON_NONE/SHIELD/DISABLED. Always override (not just if empty) so any stale out-of-set spawn weapon is corrected. Re-derive `spawnWeaponNum` immediately so the current match's player/bot spawn respects the fallback choice. Build clean 774/774. `PerfectDark.exe` 53,195,903 / `PerfectDarkServer.exe` 23,140,832. | `src/game/setup.c` | Playtest: Car Park solo sim with a small weapon set (e.g. Pistols) + enough bots to trigger the fallback — only weapons from the configured weapon set should appear, both on pads (already correct) and on player/bot spawn. Check `SETUP: world pickups ... forcing spawn-with-weapon fallback id='...'` log line names a catalog ID that is in the configured set. |

| **B-184** | MED | **ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED + FIXED-PENDING-PLAYTEST 2026-04-19 (elated-hugle-7ec221 — S384)**. Commit `fe107e3e` (2026-04-17, M4 optimisation) collapsed `ALIGN16(val)` to `(val)` — was valid for SIZE-only uses but broke POINTER uses at `src/game/gfxmemory.c:154` (`g_GfxMemPos = (u8 *)ALIGN16((uintptr_t)g_GfxMemPos)`). `Vtx` is 12 bytes, so `gfxAllocateVertices(count)` advances `g_GfxMemPos` by `count*12`; for odd counts the no-op macro leaves `g_GfxMemPos mod 16 != 0`. The next `gfxAllocateColours()` then uses `g_GfxMemPos` as the base for the `Col` array the subsequent `G_COL` command binds as `vcn`, so `gfx_sp_set_vertex_colors` reads misaligned bytes from an offset-by-12-mod-16 source — each draw call gets a consistent-but-wrong vertex-colour array, producing the per-object tints Mike screenshotted (yellow computer props, cyan elevator top, olive character faces, dark-red `env={40 0a 0a ff}` dominant on ~14% of draws in the S382.3 diag). Also explains the S382 diag "`vtx0` = `ff ff f0 f0` with `lighting=0`" rows starting at G_COL #101 — same misread pattern from a drifted pointer. Fix is the same one-line change as B-193 — `src/include/constants.h:79` restored to `((((val) + 0xf) | 0xf) ^ 0xf)`. The existing S382 `GFX.DIAG: G_COL` instrumentation in `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp::gfx_sp_set_vertex_colors` is retained; post-fix log should show `vtx0` stabilising to authored colour bytes (typically `ff ff ff ff` or grayscale per-prop) rather than drift-dependent bytes. Build clean 777/777. `PerfectDark.exe` 53,232,611 / `PerfectDarkServer.exe` 23,154,674. **[Prior-pass history]:** Four prior passes (S372 SAVED-EFFECT strip; S381 effect_normal_tint mod folder rule-out; S382 visual-evidence + G_COL diag ship; S382 fourth-pass static diff audit of the AP Phase sprint). All rule-outs stand (SAVED EFFECT dead, effect_normal_tint inert, meshDebug inert, dlights uniform-white, no G_LIGHTING clears on char/prop draws, AP Phase 3 rename byte-identical, S322/S323 IS4MB strips touched zero render state). The tint is NOT normal-visualisation, NOT UV corruption, NOT texture selection — it was vertex-colour data misread from a misaligned vcn pointer, exactly matching the "per-object consistent tint on correct textures" pattern. | `src/include/constants.h` | Playtest CI main menu + free-roam: character skin + clothing should be their authored colours (not olive-green); computer props should be their authored tint (not yellow/cyan); elevator top should be gray (not cyan); doors should be their authored colour (not yellow). `GFX.DIAG: G_COL` lines in `pd-client.log` should show stable `vtx0` bytes that match the visible prop colour. Repeat on other stages (Dam, Carrington Villa, Felicity) to regression-check. |
